chapterTitle: ریاضی حصہ اول: اعدادِ مرکب، قالب و مقطعات اور ویکٹرز (Complex Numbers, Matrices & Vectors)

questions.question: Every real number is also a:

options.C: Complex number with zero imaginary part

questions.explanation: Any real number x can be written in the form x + 0i, which is a complex number where the imaginary part is zero (R ⊂ C).

The multiplicative identity in the set of complex numbers is:
questions.explanation: (1, 0) corresponds to 1 + 0i = 1, which satisfies (1, 0)(x, y) = (x, y) for all complex numbers (x, y).

questions.question: If z = x + iy, then the product z · z̄ (where z̄ is the complex conjugate) is always:
questions.explanation: z · z̄ = (x + iy)(x - iy) = x^2 - (iy)^2 = x^2 + y^2 = |z|^2, which is always real and non-negative.

questions.question: The imaginary part of (2 - 3i)^2 is:
questions.explanation: (2 - 3i)^2 = 4 - 12i + (3i)^2 = 4 - 12i - 9 = -5 - 12i. The imaginary part Im(z) is -12.

questions.question: The modulus of the complex number z = -3 - 4i is:
If ((1 + i)/(1 - i))^n = 1, then the least positive integral value of n is:
questions.explanation: (1 + i)/(1 - i) = (1 + i)^2 / (1 - i^2) = (1 + 2i - 1)/2 = 2i/2 = i. Thus i^n = 1, and the smallest positive integer is n = 4.

questions.question: The polar form of the complex number z = 1 + i is:
questions.explanation: r = √(1^2 + 1^2) = √2 and θ = arctan(1/1) = π/4. Hence z = √2 (cos(π/4) + i sin(π/4)).

questions.question: A square matrix A is called symmetric if:
questions.explanation: By definition, a matrix A is symmetric if it is equal to its transpose (A^t = A).

questions.question: A square matrix A is called skew-symmetric if:
questions.explanation: A matrix is skew-symmetric when A^t = -A. Note that all main diagonal elements of a skew-symmetric matrix must be zero.

questions.question: If A is a square matrix of order 2 × 2 and det(A) = 5, then det(3A) is equal to:
questions.explanation: For an n × n matrix, det(kA) = k^n · det(A). For n = 2, det(3A) = 3^2 · det(A) = 9 · 5 = 45.

The inverse of a square matrix A exists if and only if A is:

options.D: A diagonal matrix with zero diagonal

questions.explanation: Since A^-1 = Adj(A)/|A|, division by |A| requires |A| ≠ 0 (non-singular matrix).

questions.question: A system of homogeneous linear equations AX = O has non-trivial (non-zero) solutions if and only if:
questions.explanation: If |A| ≠ 0, only the trivial solution X = O exists. Non-trivial solutions exist if and only if the coefficient matrix is singular, i.e., |A| = 0.

questions.question: For any two invertible matrices A and B of the same order, (AB)^-1 equals:
questions.explanation: The reversal law of inverses states that (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1.

questions.question: If A is any square matrix, then the matrix (A + A^t) is always:
questions.explanation: (A + A^t)^t = A^t + (A^t)^t = A^t + A = A + A^t, which satisfies the definition of a symmetric matrix.

questions.question: The unit vector in the direction of vector a is given by:
questions.explanation: A unit vector â in the direction of a non-zero vector a is obtained by dividing the vector by its magnitude: â = a / |a|.

questions.question: The magnitude of the vector v = 2i - 3j + 6k is:
The unit vector in the direction of vector i + 2j - 2k having magnitude 12 is:
questions.explanation: Magnitude of (i + 2j - 2k) is √(1 + 4 + 4) = 3. Unit vector is (i + 2j - 2k)/3. A vector of magnitude 12 is 12 · [(i + 2j - 2k)/3] = 4(i + 2j - 2k).

questions.question: Two non-zero vectors a and b are perpendicular (orthogonal) if and only if:
questions.explanation: a · b = |a||b| cos(θ). If θ = 90°, cos(90°) = 0, so a · b = 0.

questions.question: If |a + b| = |a - b| for two non-zero vectors a and b, then:
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides: |a|^2 + |b|^2 + 2(a · b) = |a|^2 + |b|^2 - 2(a · b) => 4(a · b) = 0 => a · b = 0. Hence a ⊥ b.

questions.question: In standard right-handed orthonormal basis, the cross product k × j equals:
questions.explanation: By cyclical right-hand cross product rule: i × j = k, j × k = i, and k × i = j. Reversing order gives k × j = -i.

questions.question: If θ is the angle between two non-zero vectors a and b and |a × b| = a · b, then θ is:
questions.explanation: |a||b| sin(θ) = |a||b| cos(θ) => tan(θ) = 1 => θ = 45° or π/4 radians.

questions.question: The area of a triangle with adjacent sides represented by vectors u and v is:
questions.explanation: The area of the parallelogram formed by u and v is |u × v|. Therefore, the triangle's area is half of the parallelogram: (1/2)|u × v|.

questions.question: The scalar triple product u · (v × w) represents the:

options.B: Volume of a parallelepiped formed by vectors u, v, w

questions.explanation: The geometric interpretation of the scalar triple product u · (v × w) is the volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges u, v, and w.

questions.question: Three vectors u, v, and w are coplanar if and only if:
questions.explanation: If the three vectors lie in the same plane, the height of the parallelepiped is zero, meaning its volume u · (v × w) = 0.
